_meta.name: NourishAI food & recipe dataset
_meta.units: Nutrition per serving (food check: per typical Hong Kong serving stated in servingSize). Recipe costs in USD per item, matching the site's base currency; food prices are typical Hong Kong prices in HKD.
_meta.accuracy: All nutrition values and prices are approximate estimates for demo and education. Before presenting numbers as facts, spot-check key items against the Centre for Food Safety Nutrient Information Inquiry System or USDA FoodData Central and cite the source.

recipes.title: Steamed fish with ginger & spring onion
recipes.description: Cantonese classic: lean protein, almost no added fat.

ingredients.item: 500g whole fish or 2 fillets (grouper, sea bass, tilapia)
1 tbsp light soy sauce (or tamari for gluten-free)

steps: Score the fish and lay ginger on and under it.
Steam over boiling water 8–10 min (fillets 6–7 min) until flesh flakes.
Pour off steaming liquid, top with spring onion and coriander.
Drizzle soy sauce; pour 1 tsp hot oil over the spring onion.
recipes.whyHealthier: Steaming keeps fat low and protein high compared with fried fish set meals.
swaps: Halal/kosher: fish with fins and scales is generally permitted
recipes.availability: Fresh fish at wet markets; frozen fillets work

recipes.title: Tomato & egg stir-fry
recipes.description: Five-ingredient home staple, ready in 15 minutes.
steps: Beat eggs with a pinch of salt; scramble softly in half the oil and set aside.
Stir-fry tomato wedges in remaining oil until juicy, add sugar.
Return eggs, toss 30 seconds, top with spring onion.
recipes.whyHealthier: Cheap complete protein plus vegetables; serve with brown rice for a balanced plate.
swaps: Add tofu cubes for more protein
Skip sugar for blood sugar goals

recipes.title: Silky steamed egg
recipes.description: Soft, gentle protein, good for elderly family members.
steps: Beat eggs with 1.5x their volume of warm water; strain.
Cover the bowl with a plate and steam on low heat 10–12 min.
Finish with soy sauce and spring onion.
recipes.whyHealthier: Very soft texture, easy to chew and digest; low cost per gram of protein.

recipes.title: Ginger chicken brown rice bowl
recipes.description: Meal-prep friendly: make 4 boxes on Sunday.
steps: Cook brown rice.
Marinate sliced chicken in soy, ginger and sesame oil 10 min.
Pan-sear chicken 6–8 min; steam broccoli and carrot 4 min.
Divide into 4 boxes.
recipes.whyHealthier: Swaps white rice for brown rice for more fibre and slower blood-sugar rise.
recipes.availability: Halal chicken widely sold in HK supermarkets

recipes.title: Lighter mapo tofu
recipes.description: Same Sichuan flavour with less oil and lean mince.
steps: Cube tofu and blanch 2 min in salted water.
Brown mince in 1 tsp oil, add garlic and doubanjiang.
Add 150ml water and tofu; simmer 5 min, thicken with cornstarch.
Top with Sichuan pepper and spring onion.
recipes.whyHealthier: Uses 1 tsp oil instead of the restaurant's chilli-oil pool; tofu adds plant protein.

recipes.title: Lean pork & veg congee
recipes.description: Warm, low-fat breakfast; cut the salt vs. shop congee.
steps: Rinse rice; simmer in 2L water 60 min, stirring occasionally.
Add thinly sliced pork and ginger, cook 5 min.
Stir in chopped greens 1 min; season lightly.
recipes.whyHealthier: Homemade congee uses about a third of the sodium of typical shop congee.

recipes.title: Overnight oats with fruit
recipes.description: No-cook breakfast, 5 minutes the night before.
steps: Mix oats, milk and yogurt in a jar.
Refrigerate overnight.
Top with fruit and cinnamon in the morning.
recipes.whyHealthier: Oat beta-glucan supports cholesterol and steady blood sugar; replaces pastry breakfasts.
swaps: Soy milk + soy yogurt for vegan

recipes.title: Greek yogurt parfait
recipes.description: High-protein snack or breakfast.
steps: Layer yogurt, fruit and nuts in a cup.
Drizzle honey if using.
recipes.whyHealthier: Twice the protein of regular yogurt; fruit gives sweetness instead of added sugar.
swaps: Seeds instead of nuts for nut allergy

recipes.title: Baked salmon with greens
recipes.description: Omega-3 rich dinner in 20 minutes.
steps: Heat oven to 200°C. Halve potatoes and roast 10 min.
Add salmon and greens to the tray, brush with oil, garlic and pepper.
Bake 10–12 min; finish with lemon.
recipes.whyHealthier: Salmon gives omega-3 fats linked to heart health; baking avoids frying oil.
swaps: Mackerel or sardines for lower cost

recipes.title: Garlic choy sum
recipes.description: The 1-minute vegetable side for every meal.
steps: Blanch greens 1 min in boiling water.
Fry garlic in oil 20 seconds, add greens, toss 1 min, season lightly.
recipes.whyHealthier: Restaurant greens often come with oyster sauce and oil; this version is light and low-sodium.
recipes.availability: Wet markets sell choy sum cheaply

recipes.title: Cold soba with shredded chicken
recipes.description: Light summer lunch with protein and veg.

ingredients.item: 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp rice vinegar, 1 tsp sesame oil

steps: Poach chicken 12 min, cool and shred.
Cook soba, rinse in cold water.
Toss with julienned vegetables, chicken and dressing.
recipes.whyHealthier: Buckwheat noodles have more fibre than white noodles; cold dressing replaces oily sauces.

recipes.title: Homemade shrimp wonton soup
recipes.description: Shop flavour with half the salt.
steps: Mix chopped shrimp, pork, egg white and a pinch of salt.
Wrap 1 tsp filling per wrapper.
Boil wontons 4 min; serve in hot stock with greens.
recipes.whyHealthier: Restaurant wonton noodle soup can exceed 2,000mg sodium; low-salt stock cuts that sharply.

recipes.title: Air-fryer pork chop rice (lighter 焗豬扒飯)
recipes.description: The cha chaan teng favourite, re-built lighter.
steps: Marinate chops in garlic, soy and pepper 15 min.
Air-fry 180°C 12 min, turning once.
Simmer tomato, onion and ketchup into a sauce.
Layer rice, chop, sauce and a little cheese; grill 5 min.
recipes.whyHealthier: About 40% fewer calories than the shop version by air-frying and using less cheese and sauce.

recipes.title: Chicken & broccoli stir-fry
recipes.description: High-protein, takeaway-style, 15 minutes.
steps: Slice chicken; coat in cornstarch and a splash of water.
Blanch broccoli 1 min.
Stir-fry chicken 4 min, add garlic, vegetables and sauce, toss 2 min.
recipes.whyHealthier: Lean protein with fibre; much less oil than restaurant stir-fries.

recipes.title: Red lentil coconut curry
recipes.description: Budget vegan curry, freezes well.
steps: Soften onion, garlic and ginger with curry powder.
Add lentils, tomatoes, coconut milk and 500ml water.
Simmer 20 min, stir in spinach.
recipes.whyHealthier: Lentils give plant protein and lots of fibre for steady blood sugar.
swaps: Serve with brown rice or wholemeal roti
recipes.availability: Lentils in South Asian and big supermarkets

recipes.title: Mediterranean chickpea salad
recipes.description: No-cook lunch box, keeps 3 days.
steps: Chop vegetables.
Toss with chickpeas, crumbled feta, lemon juice and olive oil.
recipes.whyHealthier: High fibre and plant protein keep you full; olive oil supports heart health.

recipes.title: Clear-broth lean beef noodle soup
recipes.description: Lighter version of 牛腩麵 using lean beef.

ingredients.item: 250g lean beef shin or sirloin, thinly sliced

steps: Simmer stock with ginger and star anise 15 min.
Cook noodles separately.
Blanch beef slices in the hot stock 30 seconds.
Assemble with bok choy and spring onion.
recipes.whyHealthier: Lean cuts and skimmed clear broth avoid the fatty brisket and very salty soup base.
recipes.availability: Halal beef at Wan Chai/Tsim Sha Tsui halal butchers

recipes.title: Tuna & veg wholemeal sandwich
recipes.description: Better than the convenience-store egg mayo.

ingredients.item: 1 tbsp light mayo or Greek yogurt

steps: Mix drained tuna with yogurt or light mayo and pepper.
Layer with vegetables on bread.
recipes.whyHealthier: Tuna in water and wholemeal bread give protein and fibre with little fat.

recipes.title: Light egg & veg fried rice
recipes.description: Uses leftover rice, half the oil of takeaway.

ingredients.item: 1 tbsp light soy sauce, 2 tsp oil

steps: Scramble eggs in 1 tsp oil, set aside.
Fry rice and vegetables in 1 tsp oil until hot.
Return eggs, add soy sauce and spring onion.
recipes.whyHealthier: Takeaway Yangzhou fried rice often has 800+ kcal; this uses brown rice and minimal oil.

recipes.title: Miso soup with tofu & wakame
recipes.description: 5-minute starter that fills you up before the main dish.
steps: Heat 500ml water; soak wakame 2 min in it.
Add cubed tofu, then turn off heat and dissolve miso.
Top with spring onion.
recipes.whyHealthier: Starting a meal with soup can reduce how much you eat afterwards.

recipes.title: Steamed chicken with shiitake
recipes.description: Cantonese home dish; tender and low in fat.

ingredients.item: 1 tbsp light soy sauce, 1 tsp cornstarch

steps: Cut chicken into pieces; marinate with soy, cornstarch and ginger.
Mix with sliced shiitake on a plate.
Steam 15–18 min until cooked through.
recipes.whyHealthier: Removing skin and steaming keeps fat low while staying juicy.
recipes.availability: Dried mushrooms in every HK grocer

recipes.title: Garlic shrimp wholewheat pasta
recipes.description: Restaurant-style pasta at home, lighter sauce.
steps: Cook pasta, keep a cup of pasta water.
Sauté garlic and chilli in oil, add shrimp 2 min.
Add zucchini and tomatoes, then pasta and a splash of pasta water.
recipes.whyHealthier: Olive-oil sauce instead of cream cuts saturated fat sharply versus carbonara.

recipes.title: Fish slice rice noodle soup
recipes.description: Light, gluten-free noodle bowl.
steps: Soak or boil vermicelli.
Bring stock to a simmer with ginger and tomato.
Add fish slices 2 min, then lettuce.
Pour over noodles; season with white pepper.
recipes.whyHealthier: Clear soup and lean fish instead of oily or very salty soup bases.

recipes.title: Lighter Hainanese chicken rice
recipes.description: Poached breast, rice cooked in stock instead of chicken fat.
steps: Poach chicken in barely simmering water with ginger 15–20 min, then ice bath.
Cook rice in stock with garlic and ginger (no chicken fat).
Slice chicken; serve with cucumber and dips.
recipes.whyHealthier: Shop versions cook rice in chicken fat and serve skin-on; this keeps the flavour with less fat.

recipes.title: Home bibimbap
recipes.description: Colourful veg bowl with egg; easy to vary.

ingredients.item: 2 cups cooked brown or mixed-grain rice

steps: Blanch or quickly sauté each vegetable separately; season lightly.
Fry eggs sunny-side up.
Arrange vegetables on rice, top with egg and gochujang; mix to eat.
recipes.whyHealthier: Half the bowl is vegetables; mixed-grain rice adds fibre.
recipes.availability: Korean grocers in Mong Kok, Tsim Sha Tsui

recipes.title: Vietnamese rice paper rolls
recipes.description: Fresh, no-cook, great for parties.

ingredients.item: Dip: lime, fish sauce, chilli, a little sugar

steps: Dip one rice paper in warm water 5 seconds.
Fill with noodles, vegetables, herbs and protein; roll tightly.
Serve with lime-chilli dip (avoid peanut dip if allergic).
recipes.whyHealthier: Fresh vegetables and lean protein, no frying, unlike spring rolls.
swaps: Lime-chilli dip instead of peanut sauce for nut allergy

recipes.title: 3-ingredient banana oat pancakes
recipes.description: No flour, no added sugar weekend breakfast.
steps: Blend everything into a batter.
Cook small pancakes in a lightly oiled pan 2 min per side.
recipes.whyHealthier: Banana sweetens instead of syrup; oats add fibre.

recipes.title: Steamed sweet potato & corn snack
recipes.description: The cheapest healthy snack in any HK market.
steps: Scrub sweet potatoes and cut corn in half.
Steam 20–25 min until soft.
recipes.whyHealthier: Fibre-rich carbs that keep you full, instead of chips or pastries.
swaps: Add a boiled egg for protein

recipes.title: Less-sugar iced lemon tea
recipes.description: DIY version of 凍檸茶 with a quarter of the sugar.
steps: Brew strong tea in 200ml hot water, cool.
Pour over ice and lemon; press lemon; add sweetener if needed.
recipes.whyHealthier: A shop 凍檸茶 can have 30g+ of sugar; this has about 7g or none.

recipes.title: Mango yogurt smoothie
recipes.description: Fruit-based drink swap for bubble tea.
steps: Blend all ingredients until smooth.
recipes.whyHealthier: Natural fruit sugar plus protein, instead of a syrup-and-cream bubble tea.
swaps: Soy milk and soy yogurt for dairy-free

recipes.title: Salted edamame
recipes.description: High-protein snack in 5 minutes.
steps: Boil edamame 4 min.
Drain and sprinkle lightly with salt.
recipes.whyHealthier: Plant protein and fibre, replaces fried snacks.

recipes.title: Lighter HK-style borscht
recipes.description: Cha chaan teng soup made at home with lean beef.
steps: Brown beef pieces; add 2.5L water and simmer 45 min.
Add vegetables and tomato paste; simmer 30 min more.
Season lightly.
recipes.whyHealthier: Mostly vegetables, cheap per bowl, and much lower in salt and oil than shop soup.

recipes.title: Winter melon & mushroom soup
recipes.description: Light Cantonese soup for hot days.
steps: Soak mushrooms; cube melon and carrot.
Simmer everything in 1.5L water 30 min.
Season lightly.
recipes.whyHealthier: Very low calorie and hydrating; a soup course helps portion control.

recipes.title: Yogurt chicken tikka skewers
recipes.description: Grilled, spice-marinated, halal-friendly.
steps: Marinate chicken cubes in yogurt, spices and lemon at least 30 min.
Thread with onion and pepper.
Grill or air-fry 200°C 12–14 min.
recipes.whyHealthier: Yogurt marinade tenderises without oil; grilling instead of creamy curry sauce.
recipes.availability: Spices in South Asian grocers (Chungking Mansions area)

recipes.title: Grilled salted mackerel set
recipes.description: Japanese-style, omega-3 rich and cheap.
steps: Pat fish dry, salt very lightly, grill skin-side up 8–10 min.
Serve with rice, greens and grated daikon.
recipes.whyHealthier: Mackerel is one of the cheapest sources of omega-3 fats.

recipes.title: Quinoa roasted veg bowl
recipes.description: Plant-based meal-prep bowl.
steps: Cook quinoa.
Roast cubed sweet potato, broccoli and chickpeas with oil at 200°C 25 min.
Assemble bowls; drizzle dressing.
recipes.whyHealthier: Complete plant protein plus lots of fibre.
swaps: Lemon-olive oil dressing if sesame allergy

recipes.title: Home salmon poke bowl
recipes.description: Café bowl at half the price.
steps: Cube salmon, toss with soy sauce and sesame.
Arrange on rice with vegetables and avocado.
recipes.whyHealthier: Raw fish, vegetables and brown rice; no fried toppings or mayo sauces.
swaps: Cooked tofu or chicken if avoiding raw fish (pregnancy)

recipes.title: Veggie omelette
recipes.description: Breakfast or lunch in 10 minutes.
steps: Sauté vegetables 2 min.
Pour in beaten eggs and milk; cook until set, fold.
recipes.whyHealthier: Protein-rich and vegetable-packed versus a sausage-and-toast breakfast.

recipes.title: Lighter mango pomelo sago
recipes.description: HK dessert with half the sugar and light milk.
steps: Boil sago 10 min, rinse in cold water.
Blend 1 mango with milks; dice the other.
Combine with sago and pomelo; chill.
recipes.whyHealthier: No added sugar or coconut cream; ripe mango gives the sweetness.

recipes.title: Lentil & vegetable soup
recipes.description: One-pot, freezer-friendly, very cheap.
steps: Sauté onion, carrot and celery 5 min.
Add lentils, tomatoes, spices and 2L water; simmer 30 min.
Stir in spinach.
recipes.whyHealthier: Fibre and plant protein at very low cost per bowl.

recipes.title: Tofu & pak choi udon
recipes.description: Comfort noodles with plant protein.

ingredients.item: 1 tbsp soy sauce, ginger, spring onion

steps: Pan-fry tofu cubes until golden in 1 tsp oil.
Heat stock with ginger; add udon and pak choi 3 min.
Top with tofu, soy sauce and spring onion.
recipes.whyHealthier: Swap for instant noodles: real vegetables and protein, much less sodium.
swaps: Egg or chicken for more protein

recipes.title: Oven-baked honey garlic wings
recipes.description: Party food without deep-frying.
steps: Pat wings dry; bake on a rack at 220°C 35 min, turning once.
Toss with warmed honey, soy and garlic; bake 5 min more.
recipes.whyHealthier: Baking renders fat off the wings instead of adding frying oil.

recipes.title: Black bean lean beef & peppers
recipes.description: Classic dai pai dong taste, lean cut.
steps: Coat beef in cornstarch and a little soy.
Sear beef 1–2 min, remove.
Stir-fry onion, peppers, garlic and black beans 2 min; return beef.
recipes.whyHealthier: Lean beef gives iron and protein; vegetables make up half the dish.

foods.name: Char siu rice
foods.summary: Filling and tasty, but the sweet glaze, fatty pork and big rice portion add up.
foods.tip: Ask for less sauce (少汁) and add a plate of greens without oyster sauce.

foods.name: Roast goose rice
foods.summary: Rich and fatty; the skin carries most of the fat.
foods.tip: Remove the skin and share; add a vegetable side.

foods.name: Crispy roast pork rice
foods.summary: Crispy skin means a lot of fat and salt.
foods.tip: Pick a lean meat combo or half portion.

foods.name: Wonton noodle soup
foods.summary: Reasonable calories and protein, but the soup is very salty.
watchOuts: Soup base very high in sodium
foods.tip: Don't drink all the soup and add a side of greens.

foods.name: Beef brisket noodle soup
foods.summary: Brisket is fatty and the braising liquid is salty.
foods.tip: Choose lean beef slices (牛肉) instead and leave the soup.

foods.name: Baked pork chop rice
foods.summary: Fried pork chop plus cheese and sweet tomato sauce on a large rice base.
foods.tip: Ask for less rice and less cheese, or share.

foods.name: Ham & macaroni in soup
foods.summary: Light-ish breakfast but low in fibre, with processed ham and salty soup.
foods.tip: Swap ham for egg or chicken and skip the soup.

foods.name: Cha chaan teng set breakfast (常餐)
foods.summary: A lot of food for one breakfast: processed meat, buttered toast and a sweet drink.
foods.tip: Keep the egg and noodles, skip the sausage and butter, and order the drink less sweet (少甜).

foods.name: Instant noodles with luncheon meat & egg
foods.summary: Fried instant noodles and luncheon meat make this salty and fatty.
foods.tip: Swap to plain rice noodles (米粉) with egg and greens.

foods.name: Pineapple bun with butter
foods.summary: A treat: sweet crust plus a thick slab of butter.
foods.tip: Order without butter or share one.

foods.name: Egg tart
foods.summary: Small but buttery pastry with sugary custard.
foods.tip: Have one, not three, and pair with plain tea.

foods.name: HK French toast
foods.summary: Deep-fried bread with peanut butter, butter and syrup.
foods.tip: Share it, skip the syrup.

foods.name: HK milk tea (hot)
foods.summary: Fine occasionally; condensed or evaporated milk and sugar add up daily.
foods.tip: Order 少甜 (less sweet) or 走甜 (no sugar).

foods.name: Iced lemon tea
foods.summary: Mostly sugar syrup; one glass can reach most of a day's added-sugar limit.
foods.tip: Order 走甜 or 少甜 and press the lemon for flavour.

foods.name: Yuenyeung (coffee + milk tea)
foods.summary: Like milk tea, with extra caffeine.
foods.tip: Less sweet, and not after 3pm if you sleep badly.

foods.name: Century egg & lean pork congee
foods.summary: Light, warm and moderate in calories; just watch the salt.
foods.tip: Skip the fried dough stick (油炸鬼) or share it.

foods.name: Rice noodle rolls
foods.summary: Light but mostly refined carbs with sweet soy and sesame sauces.
foods.tip: Ask for less sauce and add a soy milk or egg for protein.

foods.name: Two-dish rice box
foods.summary: Can be balanced or heavy depending on the two dishes you pick.
watchOuts: Fried or saucy dishes add oil and salt
foods.tip: Pick one green vegetable + one steamed protein (steamed egg, fish, tofu), and ask for less rice.

foods.name: Steamed fish rice set
foods.summary: Lean protein and little added fat; one of the better canteen picks.
foods.tip: Use only part of the soy sauce.

foods.name: Yangzhou fried rice
foods.summary: Lots of oil absorbed into the rice; easy to overeat.
whyItCanHelp: Some protein from egg and shrimp
foods.tip: Share it and order a vegetable dish.

foods.name: Dry-fried beef ho fun
foods.summary: Classic but very oily; noodles soak up the wok oil.
foods.tip: Share it and ask for less oil (少油).

foods.name: Sweet & sour pork rice
foods.summary: Battered, deep-fried pork in a sugary sauce.
foods.tip: Pick a steamed or stir-fried dish instead.

foods.name: Hainanese chicken rice
foods.summary: Poached chicken is lean, but the rice is cooked in chicken fat.
foods.tip: Remove skin; ask for plain rice if available.

foods.name: Satay beef noodles
foods.summary: Peanut-based satay sauce plus instant noodles: fatty and salty.
foods.tip: Ask for rice vermicelli and less sauce.

foods.name: Cart noodles
foods.summary: Depends on toppings, but the broth and processed toppings are very salty.
foods.tip: Pick radish, greens and pig skin-free toppings; rice noodles; leave the soup.

foods.name: Fish slice rice noodle soup
foods.summary: Lean fish and light noodles; mainly a salt issue.
foods.tip: Leave most of the soup.

foods.name: Shrimp dumplings
foods.summary: One of the lighter dim sum items; steamed, not fried.
foods.tip: Pair with steamed greens.

foods.name: Pork & shrimp siu mai
foods.summary: Steamed but contains fatty pork mince.
foods.tip: Balance with vegetable dishes.

foods.name: Char siu bao
foods.summary: Fluffy white bun with sweet pork filling; mostly refined carbs.
foods.tip: Have one and add a protein or vegetable dish.

foods.name: Glutinous rice in lotus leaf
foods.summary: Dense and oily glutinous rice; it's a full meal on its own.
watchOuts: Fast-digesting sticky rice spikes blood sugar
foods.tip: Share one between two.

foods.name: Spring rolls
foods.summary: Deep-fried; most calories come from oil.
foods.tip: Swap to fresh rice paper rolls.

foods.name: Pan-fried turnip cake
foods.summary: Pan-fried, with some cured meat; fine in small amounts.
foods.tip: Share it.

foods.name: Steamed greens with oyster sauce
foods.summary: Order this every time; ask for sauce on the side.
foods.tip: Sauce on the side (醬汁另上).

foods.name: Custard lava buns
foods.summary: Dessert, not a meal: buttery, sugary filling.
foods.tip: Share among the table.

foods.name: Curry fish balls
foods.summary: Processed fish paste in a salty curry sauce.
foods.tip: Have one skewer, not a cup of three.

foods.name: Egg waffle
foods.summary: Sweet batter; one sheet is a meal's worth of calories.
foods.tip: Split one with friends.

foods.name: Fried stinky tofu
foods.summary: Tofu is good, but deep-frying adds a lot of oil.
foods.tip: Eat occasionally; choose steamed tofu at home.

foods.name: Fish siu mai (street)
foods.summary: Small portion, processed fish paste.
foods.tip: Fine as a small snack; skip sweet sauce.

foods.name: Bubble milk tea (regular sugar)
foods.summary: Sugar syrup, creamer and tapioca pearls; close to a meal in calories.
foods.tip: Order 30% sugar, fresh milk and no pearls, or small size.

foods.name: Mango pomelo sago
foods.summary: Fruit plus sugar syrup and coconut cream.
foods.tip: Make the lighter version at home.

foods.name: Ice cream
foods.summary: Fine occasionally; high in sugar and saturated fat.
foods.tip: One scoop, in a cup not a waffle cone.

foods.name: Potato chips
foods.summary: Easy to eat a lot without feeling full.
foods.tip: Portion into a bowl; try edamame or nuts instead.

foods.name: Chocolate bar
foods.summary: Sugar and fat; fine as a small treat.
foods.tip: Choose a few squares of 70% dark chocolate.

foods.name: Tuna mayo rice ball
foods.summary: Light and portable but mostly white rice.
foods.tip: Pair with a boiled egg or unsweetened soy milk.

foods.name: Egg mayo sandwich
foods.summary: Convenient; the mayo adds a lot of fat.
foods.tip: Pick a wholemeal or chicken option; add fruit.

foods.name: Cup noodles
foods.summary: Fried noodles and seasoning pack; very high salt, little nutrition.
foods.tip: Use half the seasoning; add an egg and greens.

foods.name: Boxed soy milk (sweetened)
foods.summary: Decent protein but often sweetened.
foods.tip: Choose the unsweetened or 'less sugar' box.

foods.name: Unsweetened soy milk
foods.summary: Good plant protein with no added sugar.
foods.tip: A good pair for rice balls or bread.

foods.name: Boiled egg
foods.summary: Cheap, portable complete protein.
foods.tip: Add one to noodle or rice meals.

foods.name: Tea egg
foods.summary: Same as a boiled egg, a bit saltier.
foods.tip: Good snack swap for chips.

foods.name: Plain Greek yogurt
foods.summary: High protein with little sugar.
foods.tip: Add fruit instead of buying flavoured cups.

foods.name: Flavoured yogurt cup
foods.summary: Yogurt is healthy but these often have a lot of added sugar.
foods.tip: Pick plain or Greek and add fruit.

foods.name: Unsalted mixed nuts
foods.summary: Healthy fats and fibre; just keep it to a handful.
foods.tip: Pre-portion 30g.

foods.name: Banana
foods.summary: Cheap, portable energy with potassium.
foods.tip: Great pre-exercise snack.

foods.name: Apple
foods.summary: Fibre-rich, low-calorie snack.
foods.tip: Eat the skin for the fibre.

foods.name: Orange
foods.summary: Whole fruit beats juice: fibre and vitamin C.
foods.tip: Choose whole fruit over juice.

foods.name: Orange juice (boxed)
foods.summary: Has vitamin C but the sugar of a soft drink and no fibre.
foods.tip: Eat an orange instead.

foods.name: Cola
foods.summary: About 9 teaspoons of sugar and nothing else.
foods.tip: Try zero-sugar or sparkling water with lemon.

foods.name: Sports drink
foods.summary: Useful after long sweaty exercise; otherwise just sugary water.
foods.tip: Water is enough for under an hour of exercise.

foods.name: Energy drink
foods.summary: Sugar plus high caffeine.
foods.tip: Limit to one, never with alcohol.

foods.name: Beer
foods.summary: Empty calories and alcohol.
foods.tip: Alternate with water.

foods.name: Water or unsweetened tea
foods.summary: The best everyday drink.
foods.tip: Carry a refillable bottle.

foods.name: Low-fat milk
foods.summary: Protein and calcium; sugar here is natural lactose.
foods.tip: Good with oats or as a snack.

foods.name: Fried chicken
foods.summary: Tasty but usually high in oil, calories and sodium.
foods.tip: Share an order and start with a salad or broth soup.

foods.name: Burger, fries & soft drink combo
foods.summary: A day's worth of salt and lots of sugar in one meal.
foods.tip: Swap fries for salad/corn and drink water or zero-sugar.

foods.name: Pepperoni pizza
foods.summary: Processed meat and cheese on refined dough.
foods.tip: Choose vegetable toppings and thin crust; add salad.

foods.name: Chicken Caesar salad
foods.summary: Salads aren't automatically light: the creamy dressing and croutons add up.
foods.tip: Dressing on the side; use half.

foods.name: Pork katsu curry rice
foods.summary: Fried cutlet plus a thick, salty curry roux.
foods.tip: Choose grilled chicken curry and less rice.

foods.name: Tonkotsu ramen
foods.summary: Rich pork broth with very high sodium; often over a day's limit.
foods.tip: Leave most of the broth.

foods.name: Sushi set
foods.summary: Fairly light; mostly white rice with some fish.
foods.tip: Add sashimi or edamame for more protein.

foods.name: Salmon sashimi
foods.summary: Pure protein and omega-3 fats.
foods.tip: Go easy on the soy sauce.

foods.name: Salmon poke bowl
foods.summary: Balanced if you skip the mayo sauces and fried toppings.
foods.tip: Brown rice or half rice-half greens; light sauce.

foods.name: Vietnamese beef pho
foods.summary: Lean beef and herbs, mostly a sodium issue.
foods.tip: Add extra herbs and bean sprouts; leave some broth.

foods.name: Thai green curry with rice
foods.summary: Coconut milk makes it rich; vegetables help.
foods.tip: Ask for more vegetables and less rice.

foods.name: Bibimbap
foods.summary: Lots of vegetables with egg and rice.
foods.tip: Use half the chilli paste.

foods.name: Korean fried chicken
foods.summary: Double-fried and sweet-glazed.
foods.tip: Share among 3–4 people with pickled radish.

foods.name: Chicken curry with naan
foods.summary: Creamy curries and buttery naan are heavy.
foods.tip: Choose tandoori chicken and dal with plain rice or roti.

foods.name: Chicken biryani
foods.summary: Filling rice dish; oil and ghee vary.
foods.tip: Share and add raita and salad.

foods.name: Chicken shawarma wrap
foods.summary: Decent protein; garlic sauce adds fat.
foods.tip: Ask for extra salad and less sauce.

foods.name: Spaghetti bolognese
foods.summary: Reasonably balanced; watch portion size.
foods.tip: Ask for wholewheat pasta and a side salad.

foods.name: Creamy carbonara
foods.summary: Cream, cheese and bacon: high saturated fat.
foods.tip: Pick tomato or olive-oil based pasta.

foods.name: Fish and chips
foods.summary: Fish is good; batter and chips are deep-fried.
foods.tip: Choose grilled fish with salad.

foods.name: Taiwanese fried chicken cutlet
foods.summary: Huge, deep-fried, heavily seasoned.
foods.tip: Share or choose grilled chicken.

foods.name: Pan-fried pork dumplings
foods.summary: Pan-frying adds oil compared with boiled dumplings.
foods.tip: Choose boiled (水餃) and add greens.

foods.name: Boiled dumplings
foods.summary: Better than fried; fillings with vegetables are best.
foods.tip: Choose vegetable-and-pork or vegetable fillings; dip lightly.

foods.name: Hot pot (per person)
foods.summary: Can be very healthy or very heavy depending on broth and dips.
foods.tip: Choose clear broth, lots of vegetables and tofu, lean meats; go light on satay dips.

foods.name: White rice
foods.summary: Fine as part of a meal; portion size matters most.
foods.tip: Half white, half brown or mixed grains.

foods.name: Brown rice
foods.summary: More fibre and nutrients than white rice.
foods.tip: Soak 30 min before cooking for a softer texture.

foods.name: Oatmeal
foods.summary: Fibre-rich breakfast that keeps blood sugar steady.
foods.tip: Use plain rolled oats and fruit.

foods.name: Wholemeal toast with peanut butter
foods.summary: Good fibre and fats; just one thin layer of peanut butter.
foods.tip: Use natural peanut butter, no added sugar.

foods.name: Grilled chicken breast
foods.summary: Lean protein staple.
foods.tip: Marinate to keep it moist.

foods.name: Baked salmon fillet
foods.summary: Protein plus omega-3 fats.
foods.tip: Two fish meals a week is a good target.

foods.name: Firm tofu
foods.summary: Cheap plant protein with calcium.
foods.tip: Steam or stir-fry rather than deep-fry.

foods.name: Sirloin steak
foods.summary: Great protein and iron, but red meat is best a few times a week at most.
foods.tip: Pair with vegetables, not fries.

foods.name: Avocado toast
foods.summary: Healthy fats and fibre; add an egg for protein.
foods.tip: Add a poached egg.

foods.name: Salad box (light dressing)
foods.summary: Good vegetable boost; check the dressing.
foods.tip: Use half the dressing; add a protein.

foods.name: Steamed mixed vegetables
foods.summary: Aim for half your plate.
foods.tip: Season with garlic or ginger instead of sauces.

foods.name: Sweet potato
foods.summary: Fibre-rich carb with vitamin A.
foods.tip: Steam or bake instead of frying.

foods.name: Corn on the cob
foods.summary: Simple wholegrain snack.
foods.tip: Skip the butter.
